title: Federal AI use is advancing faster than complete privacy guidance
source_unit: U.S. Government Accountability Office GAO-26-107681 review of expert-identified AI privacy risks and OMB government-wide AI guidance as of January 2026
geography: United States federal agencies and members of the public whose personal information is collected or used in government AI systems

denominator.unit: selected privacy-related challenges identified by GAO's expert panel for comparison with OMB guidance

challenge_scope.value: security, data-use transparency, algorithmic-decision transparency, secondary use, consent, privacy technology, performance measurement, privacy impact assessment, workforce capability, and privacy-performance tradeoffs

sensitive_data_risk.value: AI use can reveal personal and private information in raw data sets and increase exposure through collection, sharing, or repurposing

public_control_boundary.value: people may not understand or control how their data are used in AI systems

observations.method: GAO convened an expert panel, compiled a non-exhaustive challenge list, and compared the selected challenges with OMB AI-related government-wide guidance.
observations.uncertainty: The expert list is non-exhaustive and does not estimate the prevalence, likelihood, or realized harm of each risk in a particular agency or system.
observations.subgroup: Federal agencies using AI and members of the public whose sensitive personal information enters federal data or decision systems.
observations.counterinterpretation: A documented risk is not a documented privacy breach; agencies may use controls not visible in government-wide guidance or in GAO's selected comparison.

observations.period: As of January 2026; OMB guidance coverage

denominator.unit: selected expert-identified privacy challenges assessed against OMB government-wide AI guidance

fully_addressed.unit: selected challenges the guidance addressed: workforce skills and accelerating/scaling AI with privacy protections

not_fully_addressed.unit: selected challenges not fully addressed by the guidance

coverage_share.unit: percent of the selected challenge set fully addressed, calculated as 2 of 10

guidance_gap.value: OMB guidance did not specify the types of known privacy risks agencies should consider when making privacy policies

observations.method: GAO content comparison of OMB government-wide AI guidance with the selected ten expert-identified privacy challenges.
observations.uncertainty: The 2-of-10 comparison is not a score for agency compliance, privacy performance, or risk severity; challenge definitions and guidance can change over time.
observations.subgroup: OMB guidance and federal agency AI implementation practices; selected challenge set only.
observations.counterinterpretation: Partial guidance can still support useful controls, and agencies may address gaps through laws, privacy impact assessments, procurement terms, or internal policies.

recommendations.value: update guidance or facilitate information sharing so agencies address the remaining identified privacy risks and challenges

omb_comment.value: OMB did not provide comments on the report

correction_status.value: open; GAO will follow up on actions

observations.method: GAO recommendation and status review following the comparison of expert-identified risks and OMB guidance.
observations.uncertainty: An open recommendation is a governance signal, not evidence that privacy protections are absent in every agency or that a later update will reduce actual risk.
observations.subgroup: OMB and federal agencies implementing or overseeing AI systems.
observations.counterinterpretation: Future guidance, agency controls, or technical privacy tools may close some gaps without producing a measurable public outcome in the near term.

related_sources.claim: Official full GAO report provides the expert-panel challenge list, guidance comparison, and recommendations.
GAO privacy-enhancing-technology assessment supplies a complementary implementation and resource-cost layer; this record does not pool the technology assessment with the guidance comparison.

boundary: This record identifies a federal AI privacy-governance gap between technology use, expert-identified risk, guidance, and public control. It does not establish a privacy breach, individual harm, agency noncompliance, causal trust change, political action, or successful deletion or remedy for any person.

reproduction_audit.retrieval_hash_scope: Official GAO product page used for extracted challenge, guidance, and recommendation findings; full report is linked but not retained in this record.
